pull.title: refactor: store positions as a 64 bits integer in flatfiles
pull.body: That field is the last 32-bit in flat files management that is only bounded indirectly by callers' usage (unlike the file number for instance). In the spirit of the ongoing effort to avoid unnecessarily using 32 bits integers or platform specific types (for instance #24214, #33724, #34109, #35097, #35616), i was scanning for fields it could be prudent to promote to prevent any possible future misuse. This one is a good candidate because it does not change on-disk representation, since we serialize positions as varints.

events.message:
flatfile: store position as a 64 bits integer

This is the last field that is only bounded by the usage callers make of it
(unlike the file number, for instance). Promoting it to a 64 bits integer also
does not change on-disk representation since we serialize positions as varints.
Therefore, widen them to prevent any possible future misuse.
flatfile: use 64-bit file positioning syscalls in Windows
